title: Surplus lease allocator and invoice model for momentary capacity
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: design and implement a 'surplus lease' subsystem that lets customers consume short-lived extra throughput from a global surge pool while providing clear chargeback semantics and predictable fallbacks. This ticket covers the allocator, the runtime admission rules, the temporary boost lifecycle, invoicing primitives, and UX hooks for alerts/dashboards.

Scope cut: we are not changing long-term reserved capacity accounting, nor are we changing the core quota engine for reserved-only plans. This is additive: a lease is a time-boxed allowance granted from a pre-provisioned surge pool or from elastic spare capacity.

Core requirements:
- Fast leasing path: lease grant latency <= 50ms for warm pool and <= 200ms for cold-cold allocations.
- Lease granularity: 1-second billing at min with per-request metering to support microbursts.
- Preemption behavior: leases can be preempted by higher-priority reserved traffic with a configurable grace window (default 30s). Apps receive explicit preemption signals to retry or fall back.
- Accounting: two invoicing modes: metered (pay-for-use) and amortized lease (fixed short-term commitment with lower per-token rate).
- Fairness: when pool is contended, allocator applies weighted fair-lease based on customer tier and historical usage smoothing over last 5m.
- Safety: autoscaler hooks must not double-count leased capacity when making scale decisions for customer's dedicated pool.
- Observability: per-lease traces, cost attribution per-token and per-tenancy, dashboards for pool saturation, and alerts for sustained >80% pool usage.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Lease vs credit model: we chose a lease model (time-boxed capacity) rather than pure credits to keep runtime simple and enable preemption semantics. Credits would require complex token-bucket transfers and cause tricky edge cases at preemption.
- Billing granularity: second-level metering increases billing accuracy but increases write volume to billing pipeline. We mitigate by batching deltas with a 1s commit window and an aggregator service that deduplicates in-flight reports.
- Amortized leases: offer customers an option to buy a 5m or 15m amortized lease at a reduced rate. This simplifies invoices for predictable bursty workloads but requires sliding-window enforcement to avoid quota drifting.
- Fair-share algorithm: use weighted leaky-bucket with exponential smoothing (alpha=0.2) across 5m window to avoid oscillations. Simpler round-robin approaches caused unfair outcomes during short heavy bursts in simulation.
- Preemption UX: we'll emit a structured preempt event on the streaming API and a short HTTP 409 with retry-after for sync calls. This allows deterministic client backoff.

Open questions:
- Should grace window be tenant-configurable or org-level only? (Proposal: org-level default + enterprise customers may request per-lease overrides via contract.)
- How to present amortized lease line-items in invoices across multiple projects within a single org? (Proposal: show amortized leases as separate invoice items with allocation map.)

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end allocator prototype in staging that can grant/revoke leases and emit preempt events.
- Billing events emitted to billing pipeline with per-second resolution and can be reconciled against simulator within 2% error.
- Console surfaces: pool usage, per-lease trace, and a beta toggle to enable amortized leases for selected orgs.
- Load test demonstrating grant latency SLO under 10k concurrent lease requests (target p95 grant <= 80ms).

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag gated rollout to internal customers and Redwood Platform team.
2) Beta with 5 pilot customers on amortized leases and metered leases.
3) Gradual ramp with health checkpoints and billing reconciliation audits for first 2 billing cycles.
